speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To narrow this down, are your symptoms seasonal, have you had any recent insect bites, and do you have a history of allergies or eczema?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). The classic presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, combined with prodromal viral symptoms, is pathognomonic for Parvovirus B19 infection.
